title: betula pubescens subsp. callosa
intro: Betula pubescens subsp. callosa, commonly known as Birch, is a subspecies of the Betula pubescens species, a small deciduous tree or shrub native to Europe and Asia. The leaves and bark of Birch have been traditionally used in folk medicine for their anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties, providing health benefits such as reducing fever and relieving skin conditions like eczema and acne. The therapeutic actions of Birch include stimulating the lymphatic system, reducing inflammation, and promoting wound healing, which is attributed to its bioactive constituents like salicin, a compound similar to aspirin. The bioactive constituents of Birch include salicin, betulin, and betulinic acid, which possess antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties.
